texts: good. the wind, its coldness, the blowing off the sea, the past tense and the full day-16 / Year-1 / night time all come through; the only wrinkle is that "day 16 of Year 1" lands in the slot a month-date's day would use, which no rewording can fix.

mixed: the north-wind kind and its unpacking (a wind, and north) are right, but the past tense of "was" is dropped, so the parse says the wind IS a north wind timelessly rather than that it was one on that night. Appending the time anchor puts the clause on the tensed copular path, which emits the past on both halves: "The cold wind was a north wind that night."

mixed: the striking, the Cliff Path and "at night" all land, but the date from the opening sentence does not carry over — an opening date frame is not propagated across sentences, so this event keeps only the night and loses day 16 of Year 1. Use the anaphoric form instead, which IS propagated (it works in sentence 7): "That night, the cold wind struck the Cliff Path."
good. the coming is ordered explicitly before the first hard frost, and the frost is left as a bare anchor with no tense of its own, which is exactly right for a "before <event>" adjunct.

good. the whole starting event is denied as one bundle and the "not yet" is kept as a positive expectation tag outside the denial. The one thing not recorded is that this holds as of the night of day 16 — a past perfect sitting inside a denial has no asserted event to be ordered against, so there is nothing to reword.

bad: only the group-level denial is emitted — the keepers as a body had not added the salt-bloom — with no per-keeper form, so a question about any one keeper (or a keeper named later in the chronicle) binds nothing. Make the distribution explicit with a quantifier: "None of the keepers on the Cliff Path had yet added salt-bloom to the mire-essence of their lanterns."

mixed: the eleven lanterns, the count and the Middle Row are all there, but the past tense of "were unprepared" is dropped and no per-lantern form of the state is emitted, so "was that lantern unprepared?" binds nothing. Mark the distribution explicitly so the state is stated of each lantern: "That night, eleven lanterns on the Middle Row were each unprepared."
good. both the group event and the per-lantern rule are emitted, the phrasal "went out" is kept whole rather than swapped for a synonym, and "before dawn" becomes an upper time bound.
good. parses as a fireable strength-0 rule over lanterns at the Sunken Cove, with "no" recorded as the quantifier word beside it.
good. same fireable strength-0 shape as the Sunken Cove sentence, over lanterns in the Northcove.
good. the spires, the sheltered cove and the "against the north wind" phrase all land, and the north wind is linked back to the wind of the opening sentence rather than treated as a new one.
